unresolvedReleaseQuestions.question: The single-incident fee. Section 17-22-940(G) as amended by 2018 Act No. 254 was read at source on 2026-08-06 and provides that where multiple charges from a single incident are combined under § 17-1-40 or § 17-22-150(a), 'only one two hundred fifty-dollar fee, one twenty-five dollar SLED verification fee, and one thirty-five dollar clerk of court filing fee may be charged'. The controlling review reports the single-incident solicitor fee as one hundred fifty dollars, drawn from Supreme Court expungement guidance. The current statutory figure is two hundred fifty dollars. The packet quotes the statutory figure and does not promise the lower one.

Whether the § 22-5-910(E) same-incident aggregation rule can be relied on in practice to bring several closely connected offences sentenced at one proceeding within a single application, given that § 17-22-940(G) permits multiple charges on one order only for § 17-1-40 and § 17-22-150(a). Both subsections were read at source on 2026-08-06 and are not obviously reconciled: § 22-5-910(E) treats such offences as one conviction 'for expungement purposes', while § 17-22-940(G) restricts what may appear on one order. The packet does not promise a single application on this route.

How the § 22-5-930(A) route interacts with § 44-53-450(b) for a participant who would now be eligible for a conditional discharge. Subsection (A) was read at source on 2026-08-06 and expressly includes 'those charges for which the person would now be eligible for a conditional discharge pursuant to Section 44-53-450', which brings some conditional-discharge-type facts inside the conviction route; subsection (D) separately bars the route where the person actually had a conditional discharge within the lookback period. Which route a participant with both features should be pointed to, and in what order, is a counselling question the statute does not answer.
